extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants and European patent attorneys working before the EPO
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the 2024 updates to the European Patent Office Guidelines for Examination, highlighting changed practice and procedural/substantive requirements affecting prosecution, post-grant procedure, and formalities before the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority entitlement and approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical strict approaches to formal entitlement to priority: (i) 'all applicants approach' — where a priority application filed by joint applicants requires all of them (or their successors in title) to be named on the subsequent priority-claiming application for validity; (ii) 'joint applicants approach' — where a priority application filed by a single applicant and the subsequent application is in the name of joint applicants, the priority claim is valid if at least one of the subsequent applicants was applicant or successor in title to the priority applicant; (iii) 'PCT joint applicants approach' — priority is valid if at least one of the applicants of the PCT application is applicant or successor in title to the priority applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following G1-2/22, Part A-III, 6.1 now confirms a 'strong rebuttable presumption' that an applicant or joint applicants claiming priority in accordance with Article 88(1) EPC and Rule 52 are entitled to the claimed priority 'absent any substantiated indication to the contrary.' For international (PCT) applications filed by joint applicants but without naming the priority applicant for the European designation, 'the mere fact of the joint filing implies an agreement... allowing all of them to rely on the priority right unless substantial facts indicate otherwise.' The burden of proof remains high to rebut the presumption (cases T2360/19, T2689/19, T2516/19 indicate a high barrier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of post-published data in inventive step assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-published data (data not present in the application as filed) can be taken into account in the assessment of inventive step only if the skilled person, having common general knowledge and based on the application as originally filed, can derive that the effect is encompassed by the technical teaching and embodied by the same originally disclosed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines updated (Part E-IV, 4.1; Part G-VII, 5.2; Part G-VII, 11) to reflect G 2/21. The EBA confirmed post-published data may be considered, but further practical guidance is limited and applicants will have to rely on later case law for clarification. Practitioners should ensure the application as filed plausibly and directly supports the claimed technical effect such that post-published data only confirms what is already derivable from the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed notification and abolition of the 10-day rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO's previous '10-day rule' (documents deemed notified on the tenth day after the date stamped on them) was abolished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of 1 November 2023, Communications are deemed notified on the day they are issued. Safeguard: if a document is delivered more than 7 days after its date and the EPO cannot prove it reached the recipient within those 7 days, any time periods set by the document will be extended by the number of days past the 7-day limit. See Part E-II, 2.3. Practitioners must be aware that notification is effectively same-day unless late delivery beyond 7 days can be shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary Patent (UP) post-grant procedure and UPC interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: A Unitary Patent (UP) request can be filed at the EPO within one month of grant to obtain unitary protection in participating Member States; oppositions may be accelerated where UPC infringement or revocation actions are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines (General Part; Part C-V, 2.1; Part D-VII, 1.2; Part E-VIII, 5) updated to reflect the Unitary Patent system (in force from 1 June 2023) and procedural interaction with the Unitary Patent Court (UPC). Practitioners should consider unitary validation timing and monitor for UPC proceedings which may accelerate opposition timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation states — addition of Georgia
rubrics_metrics.description: From 15 January 2024, applicants have the option of validating a European patent in Georgia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A-III, 12.1 updated. Practitioners should include Georgia in validation planning and fee/translation considerations where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing compliance and divisional handling (ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: All European patent applications filed after 1 July 2022 that contain DNA, RNA or amino acid sequences must be accompanied by an ST.26 compliant sequence listing (WIPO Standard ST.26 replaced ST.25). For divisionals filed after 1 July 2022 from parents filed before that date, the divisional requires ST.26 while the parent remains ST.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converting a parent ST.25 listing to ST.26 risks adding matter. To mitigate this, applicants may file the parent’s ST.25 listing as PDF pages in the divisional (these pages are excluded from page fee calculation) and subsequently file an ST.26 listing. An ST.26 listing must be filed before an invitation to file the same is issued to avoid a late furnishing fee. Relevant updates: Part A-III, 13.2; Part A-IV, 5; Part A-IV, 5.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for antibodies — need for surprising technical effect or novel format
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural non-obviousness arguments are rarely accepted for antibodies; to establish inventive step applicants generally need to show a surprising technical effect in the application, such as unexpected improvements in properties (therapeutic activity, stability, immunogenicity). A novel type of functional antibody format may also be considered inventive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G-II, 6.2 provides explicit examples of surprising technical effects and Part G-II, 6.1.3 provides additional guidance on defining antibodies by reference to functional features. Drafting should emphasize demonstrated technical effects and, where relying on functional definitions, ensure support in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description amendments to avoid inconsistency with allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must be amended to bring it into line with the allowed claims; inconsistencies between the description and claims resulting from amendments made to the claims during opposition must be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part D-IV, 5 updated. There has been debate and a referral to the EBA is expected, but current practice requires amending the description to remove discrepancies created by claim amendments in opposition. Practitioners should proactively align the description when claims are amended to reduce opposition/post-opposition issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency requirements for AI/ML inventions — disclosure of training-data characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally there is no need to disclose a specific training dataset itself, but if the technical effect relied upon depends on particular characteristics of a training dataset, those characteristics required to reproduce the technical effect must be disclosed unless the skilled person can determine them without undue burden using common general knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G-II, 3.3.1 updated. For AI/ML inventions, assess whether claimed technical effects hinge on dataset-specific features; if so, include sufficient detail about those characteristics in the disclosure or provide a path for the skilled person to reproduce the effect without undue burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of inventor — natural person requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must be a natural person and the EPO will check this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A-III, 5.1 and 5.3 updated. Ensure inventor designations name natural persons and be prepared for EPO checks during filing/examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of transfers of right and licences — evidentiary and procedural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1 April 2024 the EPO will accept a broader range of electronic signatures on supporting documents for recording transfers of right or licences, and will change practice concerning examination of an individual's entitlement to sign for a legal person; additionally, no administrative fee will be due if requests are filed using MyEPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted authentication: (i) handwritten signatures, (ii) facsimile signatures, (iii) text string signatures, and (iv) digital signatures meeting certain criteria. While a person entitled to sign by virtue of their position must still expressly state their position, the EPO will no longer check their entitlement to sign. Part E-XIV, 3 updated. Practitioners should adapt documentation practices, use MyEPO to avoid fees, and be aware of the relaxed signature and entitlement-checking procedures.
